The Naga Fruit supply chain had held up very well. A massive stockpile of the man-sized fruits had been built up in Arsenal - it was a sight to see, great pyramids of the tubular purple fruits ascending into the shadows at the top of the vault. From the middle of the stack, a small load of the gleaming fruits was plucked by two workers like so many rocks from a rubble mound, roughly seven in all. They were put in net bags and taken to the back of the vault, to the seemingly solid sheer stone wall that they faced.

A complex series of raps and cracks on the wall by the two workers in just the right place resonated through the vault, then hairline cracks began to appear in the rock face. They rocketed upwards towards a common point, then finally met and the stone swung inwards. They stepped onto a cliff upon a wide shaft leading straight down with a platform hanging over it. The wind from below swept and howled and chilled their bones to the core. The workers with their precious load stepped onto the platform, and they began to descend. Into the deep.

To a cavern they came, tucked away within the deepest recesses of Arsenal for good reason. Here, the drug was made - and the first batch was about to go into production. Dozens of chemists resided here, sworn to never leave the cavern except in the most dire of circumstances, for the production of this drug is the most heavily guarded secret of the Deva. The Naga fruits were chopped coarsely, then loaded into a press. The press came down with incredible amounts of force, and the juice of the Naga fruit spurted out into the collection bucket beneath it. From there, it was then poured into a funnel leading to a still pot. It boiled and evaporated under the intense heat, then passed through a filter made of a large collection of the gills from hallucinogenic mushrooms. What was left behind from the evaporation was poured off and mixed with lime to create the only known antidote - as evidenced by the extensive testing on prisoners. The evaporate passed then through a condenser, then fifteen more stages of evaporation, increasingly heavier filtration, and then condensation in that order. What was finally left at the end from all seven fruits was roughly a gallon of the deepest purple syrup in existence - the Naga's Kiss. Drip, drop, it poured into a glass jug and was loaded back onto the lift. The workers ascended to the main level again, and off they went to their next destination.

#

To the springs they went, the source of all the water in Arsenal. A cork with a tube they put into the jug, and they hung it upside-down connected to a special apparatus. The "apparatus" was a thin glassware tube leading to a blown ball in line with the tube, connected to another, thinner, tube: a rate limiter. This would limit the dripping to one drop every few hours - for a few drops a day was all needed to keep the population in line. The Naga's Kiss was exceedingly potent in its most refined form. And so the drug was introduced into Arsenal's water supply for the first time.

The other were the schematics and plans for something they called "The Simple Equation", which involved the gunpowder being used to launch heavy projectiles at high speeds. Such items and knowledge will do well in the hands of the Schryke. The difficult and arduous task of bringing the fruit to the Deva has reaped its rewards.
